stem: An education study measures average test score improvement across 3 schools, each containing multiple classrooms. school A has 15 observations with mean 67.6 points (within-school SD = 3.8). school B has 10 observations with mean 55.9 points (within-school SD = 6.9). school C has 8 observations with mean 67.4 points (within-school SD = 4.4). The between-school standard deviation is uncertain, estimated between 4.6 and 11.6 points. Using a hierarchical Bayesian model, estimate the true average test score improvement for school B, accounting for shrinkage toward the grand mean and the uncertainty in the between-school variation.

ground_truth.answer: Hierarchical estimate for school B: 56.5 points (shrunk from raw 55.9). Range [56.2, 57.4] as between-school SD varies from 4.6 to 11.6. Pooled mean: 64.0.

solution_steps: Compute pooled (grand) mean: 64.0 points (weighted average of 3 school means).
Shrinkage factor for school B: B = σ²_between / (σ²_between + σ²_within/10). At σ_between=7.7: B = 0.926.
Interval [56.2, 57.4] captures uncertainty from the unknown between-group variance.
common_failure_modes: Using the raw observed mean (55.9) without shrinkage
Using only the grand mean (64.0) and ignoring group-specific data
Not recognizing that small-sample groups should be shrunk more toward the grand mean
Treating the between-group variance as known rather than uncertain
